The Read & Publish deal keeps ScienceDirect reading rights and adds 100% open access publishing in eligible journals; a separate agreement covers Scopus access. UNL's Anton Pijpers noted higher-education budget cuts are 'putting pressure on these types of agreements.'
elsevierRelevance: This is Elsevier's own core Dutch business relationship — the national Read & Publish and Scopus agreement covering all 66 major NL research organisations — with UNL's own spokesperson flagging budget pressure on renewal, directly relevant against the backdrop of Maastricht and others already cutting other subscription databases.

title: Dutch universities drop Web of Science as costs rise and open-science pressure builds

VU cited two reasons: its Barcelona Declaration on Open Research Information commitment, and cost — renewal was expected to exceed €100,000 amid budget cuts. VU is directing researchers toward Scopus, OpenAIRE and OpenAlex as replacements, explicitly keeping its Scopus license in place.
elsevierRelevance: A four-university wave of subscription-database cancellations shows real budget and open-science pressure on paid citation databases generally — the same pressure that led Maastricht to drop Scopus. Notably VU is keeping Scopus while dropping Web of Science, a relative win for Elsevier over Clarivate specifically, worth tracking as other universities decide.

title: Maastricht University cancels Scopus license, invests in OpenAlex instead
description: Maastricht University Library is cancelling its Scopus license — Elsevier's abstract and citation database — effective 1 January 2027, citing declining usage, sharply rising costs, and diminishing unique content versus open alternatives. It is simultaneously entering a partner subscription with OpenAlex, the free open database, which will take over Scopus's supplementary role feeding UM's Current Research Information System (Pure). UM's separate license for full-text Elsevier journal access is unaffected.
elsevierRelevance: A named Dutch institution is dropping Elsevier's own Scopus product for a free open alternative — a direct, quantified competitive loss (cost and declining usage cited explicitly), not just a Clarivate/Web of Science story.
